source: sanitized Windows vendor-API hardware output-mute encoding plus live write/read-back/exact-restore validation

live_validation.procedure: with Lewitt Control Center closed, choose an output pair above -60 dB with zero state flags and non-zero DSP attenuation; set only its paired hardware-mute flags through the public encoder for five seconds; read back through the public snapshot path; restore the exact original 40-byte block; read back
live_validation.api_result: both temporary state flags read back as 1 and the exact original 40-byte block was restored and matched
live_validation.physical_output_result: user confirmed that Output 1/2 physically muted during the five-second observation window
live_validation.result: public encoder, vendor-API byte round trip, public Boolean read-back, physical mute effect, and exact restoration passed

limitations: Recovered vendor code also writes these flags when the paired hardware gain equals -60 dB; output-gain writes must therefore keep the flags synchronized at that endpoint.
The public hardware-mute control is approved only for the three paired physical outputs on Windows firmware 0x018A.
The official control center's visible DSP mute uses host-filter property 400 instead; this fixture validates an independent device hardware mute.
The underlying USB setup packet has not been captured with USBPcap.
